name: starlink_5285_skku_downlink_pass_v1
objective: Compare the BER of OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM under the same SKKU–STARLINK-5285 downlink conditions and the same received Eb/N0.

radio.carrier_frequency_basis: Representative Ku-band frequency for the four-scheme BER comparison; not a measured channel assignment for STARLINK-5285.
radio.bandwidth_basis: One-quarter of the observed 240 MHz Starlink Ku channel width for computational tractability, retaining the observed subcarrier spacing; this is a simulation choice, not the measured bandwidth of STARLINK-5285. The initial BER comparison uses all 256 bins without edge guard or DC null bins; guard/DC sensitivity studies and measured spectral occupancy remain for later.

constellation_normalization.scope: Use the same fixed constellation scaling for data symbols in OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM; do not rescale each random frame to force its empirical average to one.
constellation_normalization.units: Relative simulation energy units, not a physical transmit-power assignment of 1 watt.
constellation_normalization.note: All four schemes use the same Gray bit mapping, a data-symbol-only Eb reference, and unitary useful-signal transforms. Sampling, pilot energy, and the final waveform-sample noise mapping remain to be designed.

waveform_transform_normalization.scope: Modulation and demodulation basis transforms on the useful frame, before prefix insertion and after prefix removal; this is not a constraint on the propagation channel or equalizer gain.
waveform_transform_normalization.energy_invariant: sum(|x_useful|^2) = sum(|s_grid|^2) on the same normalized discrete sample basis. Include explicitly allocated pilot energy in s_grid if pilots are later inserted.
waveform_transform_normalization.fourier_block_rule: Scale each length-L forward and inverse DFT block by 1/sqrt(L); apply this per transformed axis in two-dimensional Fourier mappings.
waveform_transform_normalization.daft_rule: Use a unitary Fourier block and unit-magnitude chirp factors for the DAFT/IDAFT pair; this does not choose AFDM chirp parameters.
waveform_transform_normalization.frame_scaling: Use fixed analytic transform factors; do not rescale each random frame to a forced empirical signal power or energy.
waveform_transform_normalization.prefix_and_pilot_energy: Preserve pilot energy through the useful-signal transforms when present. Count energy introduced by prefixes or other added samples separately; do not hide overhead by renormalizing the complete transmitted frame.
waveform_transform_normalization.note: This fixes transform normalization only. Sampling, pulse shaping, prefix lengths, pilot allocations, and waveform-specific channel estimation/equalization remain to be designed.

frame_design.basis: A manageable first BER frame candidate using the agreed 256-bin, 234.375 kHz grid. The DD-a-OFDM reference uses 64 time symbols but a different subcarrier spacing; 64 here is not orbit-derived or physically optimal. The initial single-path baseline assumes perfect common-Doppler compensation. Frame length remains provisional pending guard/pilot and waveform-specific receiver design.

pilot_comparison_policy.pilot_plus_pilot_guard_resource_fraction: Use the same fraction of the frame's resources for pilots and pilot-specific guard or reserved cells across all four schemes.
pilot_comparison_policy.total_pilot_energy_rule: Match the total energy allocated to pilot signals across all four schemes; do not treat a higher-power pilot as free.
pilot_comparison_policy.note: Pilot-specific guards are distinct from the already-agreed zero spectral edge guard bins. The initial single-path baseline assumes perfect common-Doppler knowledge and correction, so it does not require a Doppler-acquisition preamble or estimator. Each scheme's channel estimator and any later practical synchronization design remain undecided.

baseline.purpose: First validate the four transceivers and their energy/noise normalization in a single-path LOS plus complex AWGN channel with perfectly known and fully corrected common Doppler; this stage does not test Doppler robustness.

multipath_followup.profile_basis: Agreed synthetic, LOS-dominant three-path comparison condition; not a measurement of the SKKU–STARLINK-5285 channel or a standardized NTN profile.
multipath_followup.doppler_model: Apply the orbit-derived LOS Doppler at each snapshot to all three paths, with zero additional per-path Doppler as a first approximation for a fixed ground station and stationary local reflectors. This does not model differential Doppler spread.

doppler_effect_followup.purpose: Consider Doppler effects in multipath after validating the perfectly common-Doppler-compensated single-path baseline.
doppler_effect_followup.note: The existing three-path control profile retains zero additional per-path Doppler. Any differential Doppler, compensation error, or within-frame channel evolution requires a separately discussed model and justified parameters; none is selected here.

path_phase_and_gain_realization.path_magnitudes: Fixed at the agreed relative powers throughout each frame; no within-frame amplitude fading in the first comparison.
path_phase_and_gain_realization.relative_phases: Draw a new random reflection-path phase combination for each independent BER trial and keep it fixed within that trial's frame.

phase_distribution.reflection_phases_rad: Independent continuous uniform draws on [0, 2*pi) for each BER trial.

path_phase_and_gain_realization.paired_comparison: Reuse the same initial relative-phase realization for OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM and for the low- and high-Doppler snapshots within a trial.
path_phase_and_gain_realization.within_frame_time_variation: Retain only the orbit-derived common Doppler phase rotation; do not add random amplitude evolution or differential phase/Doppler evolution between paths.

power_normalization.common_complex_gain_scale: 1/sqrt(sum_p(P_p)); apply once to all path gains so sum_p(|h_p|^2) = 1 while preserving the agreed relative powers.
power_normalization.scope: Channel-profile level, not a per-frame or per-frequency-bin received-power adjustment.
power_normalization.receiver_noise: The data-symbol-reference AWGN variance and its conditional unitary-transform sample rule are defined separately; sampling details and implementation are still pending.

noise_model.injection_point: Once at the receiver, after the LOS and any reflected signal paths are combined.

received_eb_n0_to_noise_variance_rule.reference_noise_generation: n_s = sqrt(sigma_s^2/2)*(u + j*v), with independent u,v drawn from N(0,1).

waveform_sample_mapping.condition: Use the agreed square unitary transmit/receive basis transforms on the same discrete sample grid, without additional resampling or filtering gain.
waveform_sample_mapping.note: Unitary receiver basis transforms preserve white complex AWGN covariance. Re-derive the sample-domain scaling if sampling or filtering introduces additional factors. This rule does not select those sampling/filter settings.

received_eb_n0_to_noise_variance_rule.note: Use the agreed data-symbol energy and analytic transform factors. Do not infer noise variance from each random frame's instantaneous measured power. The final waveform-sample mapping still requires the sampling/filter design.

noise_model.basis: A controlled first BER comparison; interference, phase noise, and other real-link impairments are not included in this noise model.

receiver_doppler_compensation.receiver_knowledge: The receiver is given exactly the same snapshot common-Doppler value used by the channel generator, without estimation error.
receiver_doppler_compensation.correction: After channel and receiver AWGN, multiply received samples by exp(-j*2*pi*f_D*n/F_s) to remove the common snapshot frequency shift before waveform-specific demodulation.
receiver_doppler_compensation.note: This is an ideal frequency-compensation assumption, not a practical synchronization algorithm or a decision about other channel knowledge. Future multipath and imperfect-compensation policies remain to be discussed.

doppler_comparison.doppler_value_source: Computed, not chosen: -carrier_frequency_hz * slant_range_rate / speed_of_light, with slant-range rate estimated by a 1-second centered difference; Doppler values rounded to 0.1 Hz.
doppler_comparison.baseline_snapshot_interpretation: Keep the original low/high snapshot shifts as orbit-derived inputs. Both have zero residual common Doppler under perfect correction; their BER statistics should coincide at equal received Eb/N0 with other conditions matched. They are not distinct Doppler-stress conditions in the initial baseline.
doppler_comparison.basis: Retain peak elevation and the visible-pass exit at 10 degrees as the original low/high snapshot references. First run the perfectly common-Doppler-compensated single-path LOS plus AWGN baseline; discuss multipath Doppler effects afterwards. Recompute times and shifts if the draft pass changes.

eb_energy_reference.definition: Average normalized data-symbol energy per information bit: Eb = Es/bits_per_symbol for the initial uncoded comparison.
eb_energy_reference.note: Exclusion from Eb accounting does not decide whether pilots or guards are present in the transmitted waveform. Keep the agreed pilot resource/energy fairness policy; evaluate a total-frame-energy-per-information-bit reference separately when overhead is designed.

evaluation.initial_stage_interpretation: Check basic transmitter/receiver behavior and energy/noise normalization against the common uncoded Gray-mapped 16-QAM AWGN reference under ideal processing. Similar BER is expected for matched ideal implementations; no Doppler-robustness ranking is inferred at this stage.

eb_n0_refinement.selection_basis: Select the region where BER changes or the four waveforms differ after the exploratory sweep; extend the bounds if needed.

evaluation.eb_n0_sweep_basis: A computationally economical initial scan, not a measured STARLINK-5285 receive SNR range.
evaluation.channel_coding_followup: deferred; apply the same code to all four waveforms if studied later
